concerns.text: The plan states that Pearson r will be reported only if the Shapiro‑Wilk test on residuals indicates normality. Pearson correlation does not require residual normality; conditioning its reporting on a residual normality test is a misuse of statistical inference and may lead to selective reporting.

VIF diagnostics are planned on the full feature matrix, which includes the high‑dimensional SMILES‑Transformer fingerprint (hundreds of correlated dimensions). Computing VIF on such a matrix is statistically unstable and may produce misleading multicollinearity warnings; the plan should explicitly reduce the fingerprint (e.g., via PCA) before VIF calculation.
